+// hash: 6953be40d24a9cfa   hw: d1e34203279adff4   sw: 92ecd26a1e76b3c0
+//
+// The SPARSECRAFT lines below are SOFTWARE-side: tiling and the
+// sparsity pattern. They are compiler
+// defines, not Chisel parameters, so they live in comments -- but the harness
+// parses them back out, so they must be kept and kept well-formed.
+// SPARSECRAFT workload = dnn512
+// SPARSECRAFT dense_mode = 0
+// The Gemmini instruction schedule (Sec 9o's software co-design levers). They
+// reach the build as -DSPMM_KCHUNK / -DSPMM_B_BLOCKS (nodes.py), but they were
+// NOT emitted here, so nothing wrote them into the tree and read_design_state
+// could not read them back: every proposal silently reverted to the defaults
+// the moment the state was re-parsed. Measured 2026-09-20 -- a run launched
+// with k_chunk=64 reported `[SW] k_chunk 64 -> 16` and reused the baseline's
+// sw_hash, i.e. the whole software half of co-design was inert, for the agent
+// and the CLI alike.
+// SPARSECRAFT k_chunk = 16
+// SPARSECRAFT b_blocks = 0
+// SPARSECRAFT x_resident = 1
+// The four below are RTL-microarchitecture parameters. They are markers, NOT
+// GemminiArrayConfig fields, until Phase 3 adds the corresponding Chisel
+// parameters -- emitting them as `.copy(gate_enable = ...)` before the field
+// exists makes elaboration fail with a Scala type error.
+// SPARSECRAFT gate_enable = 1
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_enable = 0
+// SPARSECRAFT granule_size = 16
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_operand = A
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+
+object SparseCraftParams {
+  val config = GemminiConfigs.defaultConfig.copy(
+    // --- L2 PE array geometry ---
+    meshRows    = 16,
+    meshColumns = 16,
+    tileRows    = 1,
+    tileColumns = 1,
+    dataflow    = Dataflow.WS,
+
+    // --- L3 scratchpad / accumulator ---
+    sp_capacity     = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    acc_capacity    = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    sp_banks        = 4,
+    acc_banks       = 2,
+
+    // spad_read_delay: 4 -> 2.
+    //
+    // WHY THIS LEVER, AND WHY NOW. T-A and T-B are both measurement-
+    // saturated at this design point, and the archive says so in numbers:
+    //
+    //  * T-B. CounterFile.scala declares exactly ONE SparseCraft external
+    //    counter (MAC_GATED_TOTAL); there is no ZBU_SKIPPED_TILES wired to
+    //    anything. And the Scratchpad hook is
+    //        mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip)
+    //        q.io.enq.bits.data := Mux(RegNext(sc_skip), 0.U, rdata)
+    //    -- it suppresses an SRAM read and substitutes zeros. It cannot
+    //    remove a mesh push, so it cannot remove a cycle, and it feeds no
+    //    counter, so it cannot remove a modelled joule. Iter 10 measured
+    //    exactly that: 50,862 cyc -> 50,862 cyc, 27.735 uJ -> 27.735 uJ,
+    //    3,073,967 um2 -> 3,125,081 um2. Pure area, zero return, REJECT.
+    //    T-B is structurally dominated here, not badly tuned.
+    //
+    //  * T-A. MAC_GATED_TOTAL is computed in ExecuteController from
+    //    mesh.io.a.bits, i.e. from the DATA, not from anything in PE.scala.
+    //    Iter 7 -> 8 replaced the entire isolation scheme (held RegEnables ->
+    //    stateless zero-mux) and measured IDENTICAL energy, -49,073 um2.
+    //    So PE.scala moves area only, and v4 is the measured minimum of it.
+    //
+    //  * Fmax is not a differentiator. GOPS x cycles is 524,285 +/- 25 for
+    //    every design in the archive (106,650x4.916, 79,433x6.6,
+    //    50,862x10.308, 62,269x8.42) -- the period is constant, which is
+    //    what area_source = "..._TIMING_UNUSABLE" implies. So t is
+    //    proportional to cycles, and pipeline depth is free on the time axis.
+    //
+    // WHAT spad_read_delay ACTUALLY IS. Despite the name it is not a latency:
+    // it is a QUEUE DEPTH, instantiated per bank and replicated across both
+    // the scratchpad and the accumulator banks --
+    //    Scratchpad.scala:584  dma_read_pipe  = Queue(ScratchpadReadResp, spad_read_delay)
+    //    Scratchpad.scala:585  ex_read_pipe   = Queue(ScratchpadReadResp, spad_read_delay)
+    //    Scratchpad.scala:311  write_norm_q   = Queue(...accType.getWidth..., spad_read_delay+2)
+    //    Scratchpad.scala:312  write_scale_q  = Queue(...accType.getWidth..., spad_read_delay+2)
+    //    Scratchpad.scala:313  write_issue_q  = Queue(...,                   spad_read_delay+1)
+    //    Scratchpad.scala:314  read_issue_q   = Queue(...,                   spad_read_delay+1)
+    //    ExecuteController:178 mesh_cntl_signals_q = Queue(ComputeCntlSignals, spad_read_delay+1)

+    // depth, so depth here buys elasticity, not pipelining. Dropping 4 -> 2
+    // removes two entries from each of those -- roughly 7k flops once the
+    // 512-bit accumulator-side responses are counted. Calibrated against the
+    // one flop-vs-area datapoint this project has (T-A v2's 10,240 mesh flops
+    // cost 72,794 um2, i.e. ~7.1 um2/flop) that is ~50k um2, ~1.7% of area.
+    //
+    // WHY IT SHOULD NOT COST CYCLES. This is elasticity in front of a stream
+    // the mesh consumes at exactly one row per cycle, and dma_wait_fraction
+    // is 0.01 -- the memory side is idle 99% of the time, so there is no
+    // burst for the deeper queue to absorb. Two outstanding responses still
+    // covers a 1-cycle SyncReadMem plus the 1-cycle pipe. ConfigsFP.scala and
+    // DSEConfigs.scala both ship spad_read_delay = 1, so 2 is well inside the
+    // supported range.
+    //
+    // WHY NOT THE CAPACITY LEVERS INSTEAD. sp_capacity 256 -> 128 -> 64 moved
+    // area and left cycles and off_chip_bytes bit-identical, which proves the
+    // kernel's tiling is FIXED rather than derived from capacity. So growing
+    // acc_capacity cannot buy a pass back (it would be pure area, dominated),
+    // and shrinking it would silently alias accumulator addresses -- a
+    // correctness failure, which is worse than a regression. Left at 64.
+    spad_read_delay = 2,

+// See README.md for license details.
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+
+/** Zero-Bitmap Unit (ZBU) -- T-B: zero-granule skipping.
+  *
+  * ==== INTERFACE -- THIS PORT LIST IS A CONTRACT ====
+  *
+  * Scratchpad.scala is harness-owned and instantiates this module verbatim.
+  * It will not adapt to a changed port list, so renaming or re-typing a port
+  * fails elaboration. Everything INSIDE the module is yours.
+  *
+  *   n   rows in the bank -- one bitmap bit per row
+  *   w   row width in bits
+  *
+  *   io.write_fire  Input  Bool       a write is landing this cycle
+  *   io.write_addr  Input  UInt       its row
+  *   io.write_data  Input  UInt(w.W)  its data
+  *   io.write_full  Input  Bool       the write covers the WHOLE row
+  *   io.read_addr   Input  UInt       the row being read this cycle
+  *   io.read_en     Input  Bool       a read is being issued this cycle
+  *   io.skip        Output Bool       this read may be skipped: row is zero
+  *
+  * ==== SEMANTICS THE HARNESS RELIES ON ====
+  *
+  *  - `skip` may be high ONLY when the row is KNOWN to be entirely zero.
+  *  - A partial (masked) write must CLEAR the bit. A cleared bit is always
+  *    safe, so conservative is correct.
+  *
+  * ====================================================================
+  * ==== WHY GRANULARITY IS FIXED AT ONE ROW HERE -- READ BEFORE      ====
+  * ==== SPENDING AN ITERATION ON granule_size                        ====
+  * ====================================================================
+  *
+  * The consumer of `skip` in Scratchpad.scala is
+  *
+  *     mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip)
+  *     q.io.enq.bits.data := Mux(RegNext(sc_skip), 0.U, rdata)
+  *
+  * i.e. ONE enable bit for the whole row. The SRAM read is all-or-nothing:
+  * there is no port through which a sub-row granule can be suppressed. So a
+  * bitmap finer than one-bit-per-row produces EXACTLY the same sequence of
+  * `skip` assertions as this one (the row is skippable iff every granule in
+  * it is zero) while costing DIM/granule times the flops. granule_size is
+  * therefore NOT a zero-coverage knob in this integration -- moving it from
+  * 16 to 8/4/2 is predicted to leave the skip count bit-identical and only
+  * add area. It is left at 16 = DIM = one row, which is the minimum-area
+  * encoding of the maximum-coverage decision.
+  *
+  * The coverage knob that IS live is the OPERAND population: the module is
+  * instantiated per scratchpad bank, so it sees A rows and X rows alike and
+  * flags whichever are zero, with no configuration needed.
+  *
+  * ==== TIMING STRUCTURE ====
+  *
+  * Read side (critical, cannot be pipelined -- the contract requires `skip`
+  * combinational in `read_addr` because it gates the SAME-cycle read enable):
+  * a single Vec index, i.e. a log2(n) mux and nothing else in series. The
+  * write/read collision bypass hangs off a separate comparator and merges at
+  * the final AND, so it adds one gate, not a level of mux.
+  *
+  * Write side (pipelined -- this is the "detector pipeline depth" lever):
+  * the w-bit OR-reduce is REGISTERED, so the wide reduce is a clean reg-to-reg
+  * stage instead of sitting in front of the bitmap's D inputs. The bit is
+  * CLEARED immediately on write_fire and SET one cycle later from the
+  * registered result. Clearing early is always safe, so splitting the detector
+  * costs at most one cycle of skip coverage per mvin row and never correctness.
+  */
+class SparseCraftZBU(n: Int, w: Int) extends Module {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    val write_fire = Input(Bool())
+    val write_addr = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val write_data = Input(UInt(w.W))
+    val write_full = Input(Bool())
+    val read_addr  = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val read_en    = Input(Bool())
+    val skip       = Output(Bool())
+  })
+
+  // One bit per row. At granule_size = DIM a row IS a granule, and per the
+  // note above that is the only granularity this interface can exploit.
+  val bitmap = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(n)(false.B)))
+
+  // ---------------- write side: registered detector ----------------
+  //
+  // Stage 0 (combinational): the wide zero reduce. Only a FULL-WIDTH write
+  // can ever justify setting the bit; a masked write leaves the row partly
+  // unknown and must clear.
+  val w_zero_d = io.write_full && (io.write_data === 0.U)
+
+  // Stage 1: carry {fired, row, was-zero} across a register boundary so the
+  // w-bit reduce terminates at a flop rather than fanning into the bitmap.
+  val w_fire_q = RegNext(io.write_fire, false.B)
+  val w_addr_q = RegNext(io.write_addr)
+  val w_zero_q = RegNext(w_zero_d,      false.B)
+
+  // Delayed SET, from the registered detector result.
+  when (w_fire_q) {
+    bitmap(w_addr_q) := w_zero_q
+  }
+
+  // Immediate CLEAR. This is written AFTER the set, so on a collision
+  // (a new write to the same row that a delayed set is landing on) Chisel
+  // last-connect semantics make the CLEAR win -- the conservative direction.
+  // That in-flight write's own result lands one cycle later.
+  //
+  // Invariant established by the two blocks together:
+  //   bitmap(r) is high  =>  the most recently COMPLETED write to row r was
+  //                          full-width and all-zero, and no write to r is
+  //                          in flight.
+  // so a set bit always implies the row's stored content is zero.
+  when (io.write_fire) {
+    bitmap(io.write_addr) := false.B
+  }
+
+  // ---------------- read side: single-level lookup ----------------
+  //
+  // Same-cycle write to the row being read: the bitmap still holds its
+  // pre-write value, so suppress the skip rather than trust it. Pure
+  // insurance -- it can only make `skip` fire LESS often, never more, so it
+  // cannot introduce a wrong skip.
+  val rw_collision = io.write_fire && (io.write_addr === io.read_addr)
+
+  io.skip := bitmap(io.read_addr) && io.read_en && !rw_collision
+}
